name: Sayama-cha

harvest.window: ichibancha, then later flushes for everyday lots

pluckStandard: sencha needles with a heavy finishing fire

transformation.note: Still a steamed green. 狭山火入れ is a finishing fire, not hojicha-level 焙火.

processing.description: Ordinary Japanese mushi. Sayama is not a different class; it is a different finishing fire.
狭山火入れ — a heavier final firing than Uji or Shizuoka typically apply. The cup is thicker and toastier; oxidation stays 0.

profile.mouthfeel: thicker than Shizuoka asamushi, not opaque like fukamushi

infusions.notes: a few degrees hotter than Uji sencha; the fire can take it

gongfu.curveException: Japanese greens go long–short–long: the first cool steep needs time, the second is quick because the leaf is open, the third lengthens again.

coldBrew.notes: Mizudashi still works; the toast is quieter cold.

water.note: Soft water, 75–85 °C. The finishing fire is not a licence for a rolling boil.

storage: Refrigerate sealed after opening; finish the bag in weeks. Keep away from hojicha so the fires do not blur.

shelfLife.note: Sealed, freezer then fridge, small portions.

qualityMarkers.claim: toast from 火入れ, not from a hojicha drum

commonFaults.name: Shizuoka sencha in a Sayama tin

compare.differentiator: Same steam-and-roll green. Sayama’s distinction is the heavy finishing fire, not a different kill-green.

summary: Kantō sencha with 狭山火入れ: thicker, toastier needles from Saitama, still a steamed green.
